deeper_dives.title: Natural Language → 3D Scenes: The Pipeline That Didn't Exist 6 Months Ago
deeper_dives.thesis: MCP + Blender + Tripo + Claude Code together create a natural language 3D scene builder — describe what you want, get a full 3D scene. This was impossible before MCP existed.

deeper_dives.title: The Autonomous Brand Machine: Claude Code as Your Entire Marketing Team
deeper_dives.thesis: Claude Code + Playwright MCP + Higgsfield + knowledge graphs = a system that generates ads, UGC, 3D content, and posts it — autonomously. One person runs what used to need a 5-person team.

deeper_dives.title: Physics Models → Market Alpha: When Scientists Become Traders
deeper_dives.thesis: 26 posts map physics/math models to trading — avalanche theory, Ising models, phase space reconstruction. The meta-insight: the quant edge isn't in finance, it's in importing models from other fields.

deeper_dives.title: The Self-Improving AI Workspace: Claude Code That Gets Smarter Every Session
deeper_dives.thesis: CLAUDE.md + primer.md + memory hooks + Obsidian + parallel worktrees = an AI dev environment that learns your preferences, remembers context, and runs multiple streams simultaneously.

deeper_dives.title: Napkin Sketch → Production Asset: The 5-Tool Creative Pipeline
deeper_dives.thesis: A hand-drawn sketch can become a production-ready 3D animation in under an hour by chaining Procreate → Magnific AI → 3DAI Studio → Move AI → final render. Each tool handles one transformation step.

deeper_dives.title: Body → Machine → Art: Real-Time Interactive Installations Anyone Can Build
deeper_dives.thesis: Kinect/MediaPipe body tracking + TouchDesigner + Unreal Engine = interactive art installations that respond to human movement. Previously needed a studio budget; now runs on a gaming laptop.

deeper_dives.title: The One-Person Video Studio: AI Tools That Replace a Production Team
deeper_dives.thesis: Runway + Kling + rotoscoping + motion brush = professional video production without a crew, studio, or actors. Direct scenes with text prompts and motion controls.

deeper_dives.title: Code as Canvas: When Algorithms Become the Artist
deeper_dives.thesis: Ant colonies, boid simulations, particle systems, and generative algorithms create art that's alive — emergent beauty from simple rules. The artist writes the rules, not the pixels.

deeper_dives.title: Why Your Agent Sucks: Architecture Patterns That Actually Work
deeper_dives.thesis: Better models won't fix broken agent architecture. The gap between demo agents and production agents is context management, memory hierarchy, and harness engineering — not model capability.

deeper_dives.title: 25 Agents Walk Into a Market: AI-Powered Trading Infrastructure
deeper_dives.thesis: Quantitative finance is being rebuilt on AI agents — not as black-box predictors, but as multi-agent debate systems that combine physics models, regime detection, and autonomous execution.

deeper_dives.title: The Claude Code Power User's Toolkit: From Token Waste to Terminal Dominance
deeper_dives.thesis: Claude Code's ceiling isn't the model — it's your configuration. CLAUDE.md, primer.md, hooks, parallel worktrees, and memory systems turn a chatbot into an autonomous engineering team.

deeper_dives.title: The One-Person Creative Empire: AI Tools That Replace an Entire Agency
deeper_dives.thesis: Claude Code + Figma + Runway + Higgsfield + TouchDesigner enables a single person to produce marketing, video, interactive art, and web design at agency quality — the creative middle class is being born.

deeper_dives.title: Prompt Engineering Isn't Dead — It Just Grew Up
deeper_dives.thesis: Prompt engineering evolved from 'add please' to a real discipline: structured frameworks, adversarial testing, llms.txt standards, and system-level prompt architecture that shapes model behavior at scale.

deeper_dives.title: The Incentive Trap: Game Theory for the AI Age
deeper_dives.thesis: Game theory isn't abstract math — it's the operating system behind every AI product decision, every market move, and every platform play. The entries in this collection reveal the incentive structures hiding in plain sight.

deeper_dives.title: The Claude Harness Pattern: Context, Memory, and Cognitive Scaffolding
deeper_dives.thesis: The most effective Claude users aren't writing better prompts — they're building harnesses: layered systems of CLAUDE.md files, skills, hooks, and memory that turn a chat window into a persistent, self-improving agent. This pattern emerged independently across multiple creators and maps directly to how production AI systems are being architected.

deeper_dives.title: MediaPipe × TouchDesigner: Real-Time Body-to-Art Pipeline
deeper_dives.thesis: MediaPipe's body/hand/face tracking combined with TouchDesigner's node-based visual programming creates a real-time pipeline where human movement becomes generative art. Multiple creators are independently converging on this stack — from spider-web string simulations to 3D Gaussian splatting to interactive music visualizers.

deeper_dives.title: The One-Person Studio: Creative Tech Stack That Replaces a Team
deeper_dives.thesis: In 2026, a single creator with Claude Code, Cursor, Blender, and a handful of AI tools can produce work that required a 5-10 person team two years ago: interactive 3D websites, motion-captured animations, AI-assisted VFX, generative music videos. These entries collectively map the full stack.

deeper_dives.title: Beyond Prompting: Prompt Architecture as Engineering Discipline
deeper_dives.thesis: Prompt engineering is dead. What's replacing it is prompt architecture — the systematic design of context windows, memory layers, retrieval systems, and cognitive scaffolds. The shift from 'write a better prompt' to 'build a better system around the model' is the biggest unlock in practical AI right now.

deeper_dives.title: Autonomous Agents in the Wild: What's Actually Working in 2026
deeper_dives.thesis: Autonomous agents went from demo-ware to daily drivers in 2026. But the gap between 'impressive demo' and 'reliable tool' is massive. These entries map the frontier: Qwen agents roaming NYC streets, Claude automating daily workflows, Kronos failing hedge fund stress tests. The pattern: narrow agents with clear guardrails work; general agents with vague goals don't.

deeper_dives.title: Art Without Gatekeepers: How AI is Rebuilding the Creative Economy
deeper_dives.thesis: The art market's gatekeeping structure — galleries, curators, collectors, degree requirements — is being dismantled by AI tools and direct distribution. Artists who adapt are finding new revenue streams (AI-assisted commissions, generative art NFTs, interactive installations). Those who resist are watching their distribution channels commoditize around them.

deeper_dives.title: Claude Mastery: From First Install to Advanced Agent Architecture
deeper_dives.thesis: Claude Code is not a chatbot — it's a programmable agent framework. The gap between 'using Claude' and 'mastering Claude' is a stack of learnable patterns: CLAUDE.md configuration, skills/hooks/MCP extensibility, memory persistence, cognitive scaffolding, prompt architecture, parallel worktrees, and multi-agent orchestration. This guide maps every layer with dated, sourced entries that track the evolution from Opus 4.6 through Fable 5.

deeper_dives.title: Red-Team Your Own Agent — prompt-injection CI from the jailbreak corpus
deeper_dives.thesis: The catalog holds both halves of a loop nobody has closed. On one side sit offense corpora and autonomous attackers — L1B3RT4S still landing on GPT-5, an agent that goes from one sentence to a verified exploit, scanners hunting exposed AI servers. On the other sit the pipes that pour untrusted text into your agent — Agent Reach reading Reddit and X, 90k-skill hubs, one-command skill installers. Point the attacker inward and you get prompt-injection CI — every skill install and harness change gets replayed against a jailbreak-and-hijack suite before it touches your keys.

deeper_dives.title: Skills That Earn Their Lines — benchmark-gated self-editing plus subtraction
deeper_dives.thesis: Successor to the harness and second-brain dives. Those stop at 'append a lesson after every mistake'. The catalog now holds the missing machinery — Microsoft SkillOpt rewrites skills only when a benchmark improves, bilevel autoresearch adds a coach loop over the worker, Prime Agent rewrites its own harness to 95.5% on ARC-AGI-3 — and, crucially, evidence that subtraction matters as much as addition: Boris Cherny's simple mode and the setup-purge post show stale rules make newer models dumber. Combine them into a ratchet that both adds and deletes rules, keeping only edits that beat a held-out eval.

deeper_dives.title: Anything With Geometry — Ink on Paper: the Pen-Plotter Loop
deeper_dives.thesis: Fogleman's ln turns any 3D scene into hidden-line vector paths, and vpype makes those paths plotter-ready. Everything else in the catalog that produces geometry — a phone scan, a ripped PS1 level, a ray-marched fractal, a strange attractor, the phase-space shape of BTC volatility, a Blender scene an agent wrote in Python — becomes a source for that one pipe. The output is a physical ink original, and in a market drowning in free pixels that is the scarce thing.

deeper_dives.title: Strategy Autoresearch — the judge is the product, not the agent
deeper_dives.thesis: Self-rewriting loops (Karpathy-style autoresearch, bilevel coach loops, Microsoft SkillOpt) keep any edit that beats a benchmark. Point one at trading and it becomes an industrial overfitting machine — the backtest is the benchmark, and the loop will beat it ten thousand times. The quant saves already hold the fix: probability of backtest overfitting, permutation tests, transaction costs and backtest-to-live drift. Wire those in as the loop's judge, and use the loop's own log as the exact count of trials — the number human quants never know.

deeper_dives.title: Ambient Executive Function — glanceable hardware for agents and attention
deeper_dives.thesis: OpenAI built a $230 hardware controller for babysitting coding agents. Someone answered with a MacBook-notch status app, and Bot Crossing turned 80 agents into characters who raise their hands. Separately, NFC stickers make logging a habit a one-tap physical act, and Sharp memory LCDs stay on for days at e-paper power. Combine them into a small always-on desk object that shows what needs you, both agents waiting for approval and your own NOW list, and takes physical taps as input. That turns 'out of sight, out of mind' from a willpower problem into an environment.

deeper_dives.title: Earned Autonomy — a three-tier router that demotes work to your own GPU
deeper_dives.thesis: Three trends in the catalog point at one design. Orchestrator-worker splits (Fable plans, Opus or GPT-5.6 executes) cut frontier spend. A 27B Qwen now fits a single 24GB card and posts agentic benchmarks that were frontier-only a year ago, while open-token share flipped to 80/20 in twelve weeks. And vendors can change the deal overnight — Anthropic killed subscription tokens in third-party tools. The agentic OS blueprint's 'earned autonomy' is the missing link: let each task class graduate down the stack — frontier, mid-tier, local — as its review pass rate proves it can.

deeper_dives.title: Every App Is Headless Now — agents that build their own control surface
deeper_dives.thesis: Chamath's claim that software IP stops being a moat once agents call services via MCP assumes the service ships an MCP. The catalog quietly shows you no longer need its permission. 'Build yourself a CLI for this program' covers apps with no API, Reverse Engineer Anything and the Ghidra-backed REA MCP explain closed binaries, and Claude Code already strips a smart TV over WiFi. Put these together and any legacy or closed tool becomes agent-drivable — and Bending Spoons' acquire-and-rebuild playbook shows what that is worth when the software is stagnant.

deeper_dives.title: Dox Yourself First — a scheduled agent that runs the OSINT kit on you
deeper_dives.thesis: The catalog saved a full attacker toolkit — Sherlock and Alien's Eye for usernames, email-to-account mappers, deleted-Reddit recovery, GeoSpy geolocating photos from plants and shadows — next to the defense: a de-dox checklist written after Meta AI inferred a creator's home from old posts, a data-broker opt-out game, the Flock plate-search transparency site. An agent with a weekly cron can run the offense against you and file the defense automatically. The same tools that took a security team now fit in one scheduled skill.

deeper_dives.title: Capture the Room Twice — Splat Scans and Song for Roots Music
deeper_dives.thesis: Roots musicians already treat the room as an instrument — testing a 200-year-old house's resonance, filming tunes on porches and in old venues, the way Lomax filmed singers in their own kitchens. A phone can now capture that room as a Gaussian splat, and Gausseous makes the splat react to audio in a browser. Record the room's acoustics in the same session and the sound and the image come from one capture of one place.

deeper_dives.title: Escaping the AI House Style — Taste Trained on the Public Domain
deeper_dives.thesis: Look at the design stacks in this catalog and the same names keep coming back: Impeccable, awesome-design-md, 21st.dev, Emil Kowalski skills. When everyone feeds their agent the same borrowed systems, AI-built work converges on one house style. The way out is the reference corpus — scrape a public-domain archive nobody is mining, like rave zines, arcade flyers, transit posters or historical maps, embed it, find your clusters, and compile them into a DESIGN.md and prompt profile only you hold.

deeper_dives.title: Melody Genealogy — Crate-Digging the Public Domain with Local Search
deeper_dives.thesis: Chance McCoy traces Shady Grove back to Child Ballad #81 and Sally in the Garden to a 1929 Brunswick 78 — by ear, one tune at a time. Sample diggers do the same hunt for producer gold, also by hand. Local multimodal search like SentrySearch already finds moments in hours of video from a plain-language query. Point that pattern at Lomax, Prelinger and 78-rpm archives with audio embeddings, and you get a tune family tree plus cleared public-domain samples, each with provenance.

deeper_dives.title: Own the Thermometer — $100 sensors as prediction-market edge
deeper_dives.thesis: A student cleared $100K+ on Polymarket weather contracts with a dorm-built weather station, and a separate trader harvests contracts already sitting at 99c. Put those next to free real-time feeds (NASA EONET, SDR-received weather satellite images, public EIA/HIFLD infrastructure data, live plane and ship layers) and the pattern is clear — the edge on event contracts is not a smarter model, it is a faster or closer read of the exact source the contract settles on. Cheap sensors plus an agent that watches the order book in the final hours turn that into a repeatable process. A student cleared $100K+ on Polymarket weather contracts with a dorm-built weather station.

deeper_dives.title: Forecast the Weather, Not the Price — gating models by tradeability
deeper_dives.thesis: Open candlestick foundation models like Kronos give you a forecast on every bar, and a hedge-fund stress test says it fails on many levels. A separate save shows the better question: a small logistic regression that predicts tomorrow's efficiency ratio (trend versus chop) and skips the choppy days lifted almost every metric over two years out of sample. Physics-flavored measures in the quant collection — Lempel-Ziv compressibility, Hurst exponent, Lyapunov exponent, hidden Markov regimes — are all measures of the same thing: is this market forecastable right now? Use them as a confidence gate on the foundation model, not as signals.

deeper_dives.title: Buying Dead Apps — the one-person AI-native rollup
deeper_dives.thesis: Bending Spoons went from $40k to an $18B IPO by buying stagnant software, rebuilding only what customers use, and compounding the margin. Public SaaS multiples just got cut in half. Meanwhile the catalog holds the full toolchain for agent-driven rebuilds — repo comprehension, reverse engineering, orchestrator/executor loops with earned autonomy, and checklists for the legal and performance gaps vibe-coded apps leave. Scale the playbook down: small cash-flowing apps sell for a few times annual profit, and the rebuild cost is the variable AI just crushed.

deeper_dives.title: Scan, Fit, Print — agents that design parts around real objects
deeper_dives.thesis: Open-source scanners (a smartphone Orbiter rig, a Raspberry Pi handheld LiDAR, LingBot-Map's video-to-3D) now produce a usable mesh of the thing you need to fit. LLMs already write Blender Python, and they can build a CLI for any app that has no MCP. Point the agent at the scan, have it write parametric CAD that references the scanned surfaces, and you get a custom-fit part on the first print. That is the step generative 3D can't do yet.

deeper_dives.title: Benchmark Your Brain — the skill-optimizer loop, pointed at the human
deeper_dives.thesis: The agent world now rewrites skills against benchmarks: SkillOpt rejects any edit that doesn't beat the eval, Karpathy-style autoresearch adds an outer coach loop, and skills log their own failures for batch rewrites. Meanwhile the catalog's learning entries stop at 'turn saves into quizzes'. Run the same loop on yourself. Your saves are the training set, auto-generated quizzes are the eval set, and an outer coach rewrites your study playbook whenever your scores plateau.

deeper_dives.title: Offline AI Appliances — one job, one box, no cloud
deeper_dives.thesis: Gemma Translator puts speech recognition, translation and TTS on a Raspberry Pi 5, and it ships with a bill of materials and a printable case. Around it, the catalog holds a 100M-parameter local voice cloner, a 3B OCR model that reads 100-page PDFs in one pass, local video search over dashcam footage, 4GB-GPU fine-tuning, and 27B agent models on one 24GB card. Together these are a parts bin for single-purpose AI appliances: a box you hand to someone that does one job, works offline, and never sends their data anywhere.

deeper_dives.title: Mission Control for 80 Agents — Conway's law meets game UI
deeper_dives.thesis: Once you run more than a handful of agents, the bottleneck is your attention, not tokens. Creative technologists are already prototyping the answer without naming it — Bot Crossing puts 80 agents on a tiny planet where they raise hands for help, AgentCraft runs them as Minecraft workers in isolated worktrees, a TouchDesigner sketch commands agents by gesture, a Quest 3 canvas directs them spatially. Casey Muratori's point that Conway's law now applies to agents says the interface and the agent org chart are the same design problem. Feed a Booking.com-style trace bus into a game-engine front end and you get a control room where structure is visible.

deeper_dives.title: One Dancer, a Thousand Bodies — Ensemble Choreography from Herd Physics
deeper_dives.thesis: Crystal Pite's ensemble pieces make dozens of dancers move like one organism, and that takes a company and months of rehearsal. Now webcam mocap captures one dancer, text-to-motion models spin out variations, and the quant collection's Ising herding model supplies the missing rule: one temperature knob that moves a crowd from noise to sudden collective turns. That last step is a market model used here as a choreographic score.

deeper_dives.title: The Album Is a Device Again — Offline Generative Music Objects
deeper_dives.thesis: Tristan Perich already shipped a symphony as a chip in a CD case. Google's Gemma Translator shows a full speech model stack running offline on a Pi 5 with a printable case and parts list. Local voice cloning fits in 100M parameters, and memory LCDs sip power. Put those together and a song can be a small object that performs a slightly different take every time it plays — the artist's own voice and stems, recombined on device, forever, with no server.

deeper_dives.title: Selling to Agents — metered data for buyers that don't have eyes
deeper_dives.thesis: Three saves describe one gap. Quality publishers block AI crawlers, so AI search cites whatever is left. AI assistants favor the sponsored option in 18 of 23 models, so they are steerable buyers. Software is going headless, so agents pick tools by speed, cost and accuracy instead of interface. x402 revives HTTP 402 so an agent can pay a stablecoin micropayment per request. A one-person owner of a clean niche dataset can sit exactly in that gap — machine-legible, crawler-reachable, and metered.

deeper_dives.title: The AI Capex Stack — reading it like a credit analyst
deeper_dives.thesis: An ex-Morgan Stanley structurer explains that CoreWeave-style GPU loans have a thin tail: loan, contract and GPU useful life are nearly the same length, so the bull case rests on hourly rental prices after contracts end. Other saves price that number from the demand side: open weights flipped to about 80% of token volume in 12 weeks, DeepSeek serves near-frontier agents at $0.28 per million tokens, a 27B model runs on one gaming GPU, and a $200 subscription buys about $7,000 of API usage. Token deflation is a direct input to post-contract GPU rental rates, and nobody in the catalog connects them.

deeper_dives.title: Who's Across the Table — forensics for the system trading against you
deeper_dives.thesis: Across the catalog, the systems you interact with are quietly optimizing against you: a puzzle game runs an on-device XGBoost model to time difficulty to your ad value, overnight and intraday returns run as a decades-long sawtooth, a bedroom spoofer tripped depth-reading algorithms in the 2010 Flash Crash, wash trading inflates crypto volume, and exchanges sold speed to HFTs. Agent-plus-Ghidra decompilation and cheap tick data mean one person can now audit the counterparty instead of guessing about it.

deeper_dives.title: Mocap as Reward — teaching cheap robots to move like you
deeper_dives.thesis: The Microduck RL demo shows the classic failure: a loose reward function makes the robot 'stand' in a way nobody intended. The catalog also holds the fix, scattered across collections. FreeMoCap turns a webcam into markerless motion capture, HY-Motion produces motion from text on robot skeletons, and Blender plus a GPU contact solver can rehearse physical contact. Use captured or generated motion as an imitation reward on a cheap open robot. The reward-design trial and error becomes 'show it what you mean'.
